snippet.title: The First Moonwalk - Bill Bailey - The Apollo Theatre - New York -  1955
snippet.description:
This is one of the first ever moonwalks on film
 Bill Bailey tapping to a rather quiet instrumental version of the Larks' hit "The World is Waiting for Sunrise" performed by the Paul Williams Quartet.

He's the brother of singer Pearl Bailey, but he has nothing to do with her signature song "Won't You Come Home Bill Bailey" which is a very old standard dating back to 1902.

Bill's frequently credited with "inventing" the "moonwalk" because of a tapdancing move called "backslide" which he does in this filmed performance.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Inspires Gold 😍 Varfolomeev's Ball Routine at Paris 2024 | Music Monday
snippet.description:
📺 Re-live ALL the incredible #Paris2024 action: ➡️ https://oly.ch/P24Replays

At the Paris 2024 Olympics, German rhythmic gymnast Darja Varfolomeev brought Michael Jackson back to the stage. In her ball routine, she performed to Jackson’s “In the Closet”, wowing both the jury and the crowd. She earned the highest score (36.450 points) which ultimately led to Germany’s first-ever gold medal in rhythmic gymnastics.
